title: The Quantum Stack and the Countdown to Q-Day
gist: A short podcast teaser framing quantum computing as a live geopolitical race toward 'Q-Day' (the point quantum computers can break current cryptography), featuring guests from IonQ, Booz Allen, and GDIT discussing post-quantum cryptography, competing hardware approaches, and U.S. talent and supply-chain risk.

insights.claim: The episode's framing thesis is that quantum computing hype obscures a real, advancing technology with genuine geopolitical stakes tied to 'Q-Day' — the point at which quantum computers can break current encryption — requiring a shift to post-quantum cryptography.
insights.speaker: Cameron Chehreh, JD Dulny, Ben Gianni, and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: Frames post-quantum cryptography migration as an urgent, near-term compliance and infrastructure spend category rather than a distant theoretical concern — relevant to cybersecurity and defense-IT vendors positioning for Q-Day readiness contracts.
insights.quote: Quantum’s hype obscures a reality with real geopolitical stakes: the technology works and is advancing every day.
insights.locator: Quantum’s hype obscures a reality with real geopolitical stakes...

insights.claim: The discussion identifies talent gaps and fragile supply chains as key reasons the United States could fall behind in the quantum computing race, alongside competing hardware modalities and emerging use cases as separate discussion threads.
insights.speaker: Cameron Chehreh, JD Dulny, Ben Gianni, and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: Flags talent and supply-chain fragility — not just raw R&D funding — as the binding constraint on U.S. quantum competitiveness, a signal for where policy and investment intervention (workforce pipelines, component sourcing) may be most impactful.
insights.quote: why talent gaps and fragile supply chains mean the United States could be at risk of falling behind
insights.locator: They cover the shift to post-quantum cryptography...

source_meta.author: Cameron Chehreh, JD Dulny, Ben Gianni, and Jonathan Panter
